messages.subject: AR1-besag model with gaps in temporal coverage
messages.subject_clean: AR1-besag model with gaps in temporal coverage
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

I am attempting to fit a binomial space-time model using an AR1 latent model with a besag grouping model. Training data are entirely missing for significant stretches of the time series. There are 29 time points across which I want to make predictions, with data entirely absent for time points 2–10, 12–18, and 28–29.

The model is structured as follows:

y ~ -1 + b0 + f(ID.year, model = "ar1", replicate = as.integer(demo),

    group = as.integer(as.factor(space_group)), control.group = list(model = "besag", graph = mat, scale.model = TRUE), values = unique(ID.year))

(“demo” refers to a demographic variable; I want separate estimates for each level of this variable, although this doesn’t seem to affect the behavior described below.)

The resulting model tracks the training data well but the temporal effects show surprising behavior in the years without data. I had expected that the model would show reasonable interpolation in the gap years, especially since rho is estimated to be high (0.991). However, the estimated temporal effects in gap years are always very high relative to the years with data. I suspect that this is related to the sum-to-zero constraint in the besag model, as an otherwise-identical model without the besag grouping model does not show the same behavior. Does this interpretation seem reasonable, and if so, is there a way around it? I have tried an RW1 model in place of AR1, and this works for small data subsets but struggles to fit our entire data set.

I seem to be unable to attach a screenshot to illustrate the problem, but am happy to share figures via email.

Thank you in advance for your assistance,

Chris Schmidt

messages.body_plain:
if you have missing time-points in the series, like

time=c(1,2,5,6,9)

and you want 1:9, then you need to add those in the 'values' argument

f(time, model="ar1", values=1:9)

which assign the 'values' for which the model is defined.

Let me know if this does no answer your question.

Best
H

Thank you for these suggestions. I have sorted the data table by both the time and space variables, prior to creation of the data stack, but with the same result. I had also previously tried a besag model with an ar1 grouping model, but that model strangely seems to lose the temporal component, as predictions are flat over time. I will try this again after sorting by time, to confirm this behavior.

I had thought that the besag model has a sum-to-zero constraint by default, as the documentation (from inla.doc("besag")) lists TRUE as the default value for "constr". Does this not apply when it is used as the grouping model?

Thank you again for your help,
Chris

y ~ -1 + b0 + f(space_group, model = 'besag', replicate = as.integer(demo), graph = mat, group = as.integer(ID.year), control.group = list(model = 'ar1'), values = unique(space_group))

For both this and the original model described in the first post, I am using default priors. Do you see anything wrong with this specification?

Thank you,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

if you use expand.factor.strategy = 'inla', you are kind of asking for
large marginal stdev's, as it do the expansion so you, by purpose,
create confounding, so only certain contrasts are likelihood
identifiable.

I see your concern as you want one coefficient for each effect. By
default lm() and glm() remove one level of the factor to make it
likelihood identifiable. Another approach is this one, which might be
what you want.

H

messages.subject: scale of GEV shape parameter 'xi'
messages.subject_clean: scale of GEV shape parameter 'xi'
messages.body_plain:
I understand that the GEV shape parameter 'xi' is used internally with a scale 'gev.scale.xi' defaulting to 0.01. However when I sample the hyperparams for a model with "gev" family, I guess that the simulated value is rather 0.1 * xi. This seems to be true whatever be the value of 'scale' passed to 'inla'.

Best

rgev <-  function(n = 1, xi = 0, mu = 0.0, sd = 1.0) {
    u <- runif(n)
    if (xi == 0) x <- -log(-log(u))
    else x = ((-log(u))^(-xi) - 1.0) / xi
    x * sd + mu
}
n <- 300; set.seed(12)
z <- rnorm(n)
sd.y <- 0.1
xi <- 0.1
y <- 1 + z + rgev(n, xi = xi, sd = sd.y)
r <- inla(y ~ 1 + z, data = data.frame(y, z),
          family = "gev")
myPost <- inla.hyperpar.sample(n = 3000, result = r)
c("sampled" = sd(myPost[ , 2]),
  "summary" = r$summary.hyperpar["tail", "sd"])

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

sorry, this is a pretty basic questions, but I'm wondering what people would suggest as model diagnostics for a binomial GLMM fitted in INLA.

I'm particularly interested in how well the model fits the data, and not so much in comparing it to alternative models (which I understand I could do with cpo, dic etc.).
I'm struggling a little bit with the fact that the model is a logistic regression which makes it somewhat difficult to understand in how far the methods for, say, Gaussian models are appropriate.

The model has the following structure:

fit <- inla(formula = binary_response ~ pred1 + pred2 + f(rand1, model = "iid"),
                 data = dat, family =  "binomial",
                 control.family = list(control.link=list(model = "logit"),
                  control.inla = list(correct = TRUE),
                  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo=TRUE, waic = TRUE, po=TRUE,      config=TRUE))

Any suggestions on how to do model diagnostics in INLA would be very much appreciated.

Thanks in advance,
Martin

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm trying to run a zero-inflated model. How can I add a variable to the zero-inflation component in inla?
For example, in glmmTMB I could run this code for zero-inflated negative binomial:
model<-glmmTMB(outcome~var1+offset(log(E))+(1|area), ziformula=~var2,family="nbinom2" ...)
so, var1 is in the conditional model and var2 in the zero-inflation model
How can I get something similar with inla?
I would also like to know how to obtain the intercepts of the random effect (area) in inla, similarly to ranef(model)

messages.subject: Correct formula for a spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model?
messages.subject_clean: Correct formula for a spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model?
messages.body_plain:
Dear List and Dr. Havard Rue:

I am trying to fit a spatiotemporally varying coefficient regression model. I have a set of panel data that runs for 7 years with 170 spatial units on an irregular lattice. The neighborhood adjacency file (queen contiguity) is created as gb.adj. The original model with the Y as the dependent variable, and X1, X2, X3, X4 (so named in the data table) as covariates plus an intercept.

So the regression model takes the form:

Y = 1 + X1 + X2 + X3 + X4

Instead of running a spatial panel regression analysis or a spatially varying coefficient panel regression model, I read in the Blangiardo and Cameletti's <Spatial and Spatio-temporal Bayesian Models with R-INLA> that I might actually be able to produce regression coefficients that vary both spatially and temporally (as in Chapter 7 of the referred book for the four types of spatio-temporal interactions). I organized my data in such a way so that the region ID ran faster and the temporal ID ran slower as in:

id.region id.time
1            1
2            1
3            1
4            1
5            1
......
1            2
2            2
3            2
4            2
5            2
...

All the region ID and time ID are replicated five times for the intercept and the four covariates.

But then I am lost on how to actually produce an effective formula to obtain the spatiotemporally varying coefficients since my model is "Gaussian" with covariates, the model in the book is "poisson" without covariates. Still, I try to replicate what I learned from the book and communication with Dr. Havard Rue and conjured a formula like this:

fm.stv<- Y ~ f(id.region.int <http://id.region.int>, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.int <http://id.time.int>, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
             f(id.region.X1, X1, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.X1, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
             f(id.region.X2, X2, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.X2, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
             f(id.region.X3, X3, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.X3, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
             f(id.region.X4, X4, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.X4, control.group = list(model = "ar1"))

mod.stv.intIV <- inla(fm.stv,family="gaussian",data=stv.data,
                  control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
                  control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

The run time varies quite a bit from a few minutes to sometimes hours (especially when using the "besagproper" model). It would produce results, but when I tried to extract the random effects from the model, and followed the code to produce the spatiotemporally varying coefficients for each time period and spatial units, the results seemed to be rather unrealistic.

I suspect that I might not specify the spatio-temporal model correctly (I tried to use "rw2" for the control.group, which runs faster, but the results are not ideal, either). My questions are:

1. Is this the correct way to specify a formula for estimating the spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model, assuming that the coefficients indeed interact in both space and time (in such scenarios that the changes of one location's covariates will not only have influences on the outcome of that location, but on neighboring locations in both space and time in an autocorrelated manner)?

2. What other models (except for "bym", "besag", "besagproper" for the spatial, and "ar1" or "rw1", "rw2" models for the temporal (control group)) can be used to produce spatio-temporally varying coefficients?

Thank you very much for this excellent package that has so much potential for a lot of social science problems.

Best,
Danlin Yu

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Correct formula for a spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model?
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] Correct formula for a spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model?
messages.body_plain:
to use f() as a varying regression coefficient, then we use

	f(idx, x, model=..)

which creates f[idx] * x[idx] as the effect, instead of just f[idx].
that seems correct.

be aware when using models that default have constr=TRUE, like

	f(idx, x, model="rw2")

as then the coefficients sum to zero and this is not what you want, so
then add constr=FALSE.

you can order your data in any way you like, its all about

	f(idx,x, ..., group=g)

as the i'th data point has contribution from idx[i], x[i] and g[i].

and recall 'g' are integers from 1, 2, ..., n.groups

I would guess that 'bym', 'bym2' models are not what you want, and doing
a kronecker product with the AR1 is a little strange. try model='besag'
and add scale.model=TRUE, and then use the ar1 group model.

'besag.proper' I do not like much...

for the time, the 'ar1' is the default choice for group, and come with
one hyperparameter.

If you're concerned about speed, then use

	control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive")

and check out the PARDISO library

	inla.pardiso()

assuming you're using Linux or Mac (not avail on Win yet)

H

messages.subject: Binomial Spatio-temporal model won't fit
messages.subject_clean: Binomial Spatio-temporal model won't fit
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to fit an spde spatio-temporal model with binomial response data. Its large spatial data (continental scale) with the mesh varying across the year with a cyclic ar1 structure. I can get the model to fit with a mesh that has fairly large triangles (max edge for the internal triangles=3) and coarse temporal structure (k=12). However, if I try to make either component finer (e.g., max edge=0.5 or k=52) the model crashes without giving a specific error. Running with verbose=T doesn't show any obvious warnings. I have already played round with the priors a lot along with triangle shapes, etc.

I am wondering if the problem could be complete separation? The proportion of positive cases varies throughout the year, reaching a peak of about 30% positive cases in the fall, but falling to near 0 in the spring. Could this be the reason I can't make either the spatial or temporal mesh too fine and still get the model to fit?

messages.subject: General Methodology Questions
messages.subject_clean: General Methodology Questions
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to learn the inner workings of INLA and the SPDE approach to spatial statistics. I have a couple methodology questions and I hope this is an okay place to ask them.

For now, I am just looking at the simple model

Y = X + epsilon

where X~N(0, Q(theta)^-1) are the spatial effects and epsilon is a random error term. My interest is in making inferences/predictions about X. I have two questions (or at least these are the two biggest right now :) ).

1) Is it reasonable in some scenarios to draw MCMC samples  from p(theta | Y) and use these for Monte Carlo integration to obtain p(X_i | Y)? I am trying to reach into the multivariate spatial setting, where 'theta' may contain p x p covariance matrices for p around 50. I am worried about the ability of quasi-Newton methods to explore this space, but potentially it won't be too difficult to draw samples from the distribution.

2) Now let's say I either have a batch of samples from p(theta|Y), or a set of points and weights from the quasi-Newton method, and want to make inferences about X_i. Do I just perform the numerical integration for some grid of X_i values for a numerical estimate of the posterior, or is there some more efficient way?

Cheers!
Paul

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

some brief thoughts:
1) Yes, doing the full INLA method with all those covariance parameters would be difficult, both in the optimisation and deterministic integration stages.
If the optimisation could find a reasonable mode, you could potentially use some form of importance sampling Monte Carlo integration with respect to theta, but likely the optimisation itself would be a problem, and mcmc needed to explore the posterior for theta.

2) This stage is much easier. In your example, the conditional posterior for X given theta is also Gaussian (if epsilon is Gaussian), so you can compute everything;
When you have samples theta_k ~ p(theta|Y), k=1,...,K, then
  \int p(X|\theta,Y) p(\theta|Y) d\theta
can be approximated by
  \sum_k p(X|\theta_k,Y) / K,
which describes a mixture of multivariate Gaussians, with mean and precision known.
The details will depend on what properties of that multivariate mixture you need.

Conditional Gaussian posteriors (see the 2005 Rue&Helf GMRF book):
  m_x = prior expectation for x
  Q_x = prior precision for x, conditionally on theta
  Q_e = prior precision for e, conditionally on theta
Linear observations for some sparse matrix A (basis function evaluations in SPDE/GMRF models, for example, but more generally the linear model design matrix):
  y = A x + e
Conditional Posterior, x|y,\theta:
  Q_{x|y,\theta} = Q_x + A' Q_e A
   m_{x|y,\theta} = mu_x + Q_{x|y,\theta}^{-1} A' Q_e (y - A m_x)

Now, if you need this for other observation likelihoods than Normal, but you have managed to sample from p(theta|Y), you can still in principle use the conditional Laplace approximation for integrating out components of x to get better marginal posteriors than just using the Hessian in the equations above.  Lots more details depending on the specific model/context, but hopefully that gives some food for thought!

Finn

Finn

Dear Dr. Havard:

These are extremely helpful instructions. A few more questions follow:

1. Other than model "rw2" that default to sum the coefficients to zero
(constr = TRUE), will the spatial models such as "besag", "bym", also
default to sum the coefficients to zero as well? Or will it be safe to
just set constr = FALSE for all the models just to make sure that the
coefficients are not sum to zero.

2. I added the control.inla = list(strategy = "adaptive") in INLA's
parameter list, but the calibration is still taking way too long (past
the hour mark). I signed up for the PARDISO library last night with my
school email address, but did not receive the license file, and now I
realized that I am a windows PC user, so that probably will not matter
much since I cannot use it anyways. Any timeline that it will be
available on Windows machines? If not, I'll see if I can use a Linux
shell on the windows to make it work.

Thank you very much for all the pointers.

Best,

Danlin

On 11/10/2020 4:05 AM, Helpdesk wrote:
>
> to use f() as a varying regression coefficient, then we use
>
> 	f(idx, x, model=..)
>
> which creates f[idx] * x[idx] as the effect, instead of just f[idx].
> that seems correct.
>
> be aware when using models that default have constr=TRUE, like
>
> 	f(idx, x, model="rw2")
>
> as then the coefficients sum to zero and this is not what you want, so
> then add constr=FALSE.
>
>
> you can order your data in any way you like, its all about
>
> 	f(idx,x, ..., group=g)
>
> as the i'th data point has contribution from idx[i], x[i] and g[i].
>
> and recall 'g' are integers from 1, 2, ..., n.groups
>
>
> I would guess that 'bym', 'bym2' models are not what you want, and doing
> a kronecker product with the AR1 is a little strange. try model='besag'
> and add scale.model=TRUE, and then use the ar1 group model.
>
> 'besag.proper' I do not like much...
>
>
> for the time, the 'ar1' is the default choice for group, and come with
> one hyperparameter.
>
>
> If you're concerned about speed, then use
>
> 	control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive")
>
> and check out the PARDISO library
>

>
> assuming you're using Linux or Mac (not avail on Win yet)

> H

messages.subject: temporal correlation within groups
messages.subject_clean: temporal correlation within groups
messages.body_plain:
I would like to confirm the proper way to specify INLA when modeling temporal correlation specific to different members of a group of interest.

Here is sample code from a vignette of the glmmTMB package:

library(MASS)
library(glmmTMB)
library(INLA)

### generate data set ###

simid <- function(g, n=6, rho=0.7) {
  x <- mvrnorm(mu = rep(0,n),
               Sigma = rho ^ as.matrix(dist(1:n)) )   ## Simulate the process
  y <- x + rnorm(n)                               ## Add measurement noise
  times <- factor(1:n)
  id <- factor(rep(g,n)) ### create subjects in the group
  data.frame(y, times, id)
}
simid(1)
dat1 <- do.call("rbind", lapply(1:1000, simid) )

### run glmmTMB and INLA AR1 models, with uniform hyperprior for the latter ###

tmb.1 <- glmmTMB(y ~ ar1(times + 0 | id), data=dat1)

UN.prior = "expression:
  log_dens = 0 - log(2) - theta / 2;
  return(log_dens);
"
inla.1 <- inla(y ~ f(times, replicate=id, model="ar1", hyper=UN.prior),
               data=dat1 %>% mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))))

The results appear to be very similar (INLA captures a similar intercept and a mean Rho estimate of .693, +/- .028).

Is this INLA model correctly specified? I note, for example, that I used "replicate=" rather than "group=" within the AR1 function. The latter takes forever to run and perhaps is just wrong / unnecessary here. Are there any other flags or options that might be worth investigating when specifying temporal correlations relative to members of a single group in this manner?

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] temporal correlation within groups
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] temporal correlation within groups
messages.body_plain:
it seems correct to me (compared to how you generate them). yes, group
is the wrong thing, as you really replicate the data (independently),
they are not dependent over different 'id' (which 'group' can capture).

H

On Thu, 2020-11-12 at 12:19 -0600, Jonathan Judge wrote:
> I would like to confirm the proper way to specify INLA when modeling
> temporal correlation specific to different members of a group of
> interest.
> Here is sample code from a vignette of the glmmTMB package:
>
> library(MASS)
> library(glmmTMB)
> library(INLA)
>
> ### generate data set ###
>
> simid <- function(g, n=6, rho=0.7) {
>   x <- mvrnorm(mu = rep(0,n),
>                Sigma = rho ^ as.matrix(dist(1:n)) )   ## Simulate the
> process
>   y <- x + rnorm(n)                               ## Add measurement
> noise
>   times <- factor(1:n)
>   id <- factor(rep(g,n)) ### create subjects in the group
>   data.frame(y, times, id)
> }
> simid(1)
> dat1 <- do.call("rbind", lapply(1:1000, simid) )
>
> ### run glmmTMB and INLA AR1 models, with uniform hyperprior for the
> latter ###
>
> tmb.1 <- glmmTMB(y ~ ar1(times + 0 | id), data=dat1)
>
> UN.prior = "expression:
>   log_dens = 0 - log(2) - theta / 2;
>   return(log_dens);
> "
> inla.1 <- inla(y ~ f(times, replicate=id, model="ar1",
> hyper=UN.prior),
>                data=dat1 %>% mutate(id =
> as.integer(as.character(id))))
>
> The results appear to be very similar (INLA captures a similar
> intercept and a mean Rho estimate of .693, +/- .028).
>
> Is this INLA model correctly specified? I note, for example, that I
> used "replicate=" rather than "group=" within the AR1 function. The
> latter takes forever to run and perhaps is just wrong / unnecessary
> here. Are there any other flags or options that might be worth
> investigating when specifying temporal correlations relative to
> members of a single group in this manner?
>
> Thank you.

> --

messages.subject: Effect estimates dependent on prediction points
messages.subject_clean: Effect estimates dependent on prediction points
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am testing
some models with non-stationary spatial random effects to predict an outcome
variable on a dense grid of prediction points. This to generate a raster map of
model predictions. I need a dense grid as some fixed effects vary considerably over
short distances, but due to computational limitations estimating the whole
prediction grid at once is not possible.

I tried to get
around this by splitting the prediction grid into several parts, and doing
prediction while fitting to all points with known values (training set)for the outcome
variable for each grid part separately. Afterwards I combined them again, thinking that using the same training set would produce the same model every time regardless of the prediction points added. However,
I noticed that the fixed parameter mean estimates differ slightly but noticeably in
the models linked to each grid part depending on which prediction points I add.
Between different sets some fixed parameter estimates vary to up to 1.7%. While this was in itself not too worrying, I decided to compare the estimates of one of the prediction sets to estimates

Hi,

with so few data there will be a confounding with the intercept and the
spde, and with two of those and a scaling, yes, this can happen. You
have to tighten the model up, either more strict prior for the scaling
or some kind of constr of the spde

you can consider to add constr=T

spde=inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,prior.range = c(2,.1),prior.sigma =
c(1,.5), constr=TRUE)

then scaling is essentially, a different precision for the second
replicate. I don't know if this make sense or not for you.

otherwise, I would suggest to use

       control.inla = list(strategy = "adaptive"),
       num.threads = "2:1")

and the num.threads argument have now changed in the recent versions.

... also upgrade to R-4.0 and the newest testing version, which will
also be much faster ;-)

All the best
H

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

You cannot fit the model with slm.inla or the slm latent effect because term \alpha_i needs to be inside the slm latent effect. If you take it outside then I believe that you will be able to fit the resulting model if you define matrix W with care. The model would become:

y_{it} = (I - \rho W)^{-1} (X_{it}\beta + \epsilon_{it} ) + \alpha_{I}

Not sure if this is what you want to do… Also, the slm latent effect is still experimental.

Best,

Virgilio

Got it.

>I would have the spatial index with repeated values as needed, and then the panel index with repeated values as well. This is probably the simplest solution.

It works.

If I understand well, for a dynamic model with both a spatial lag on the dependent variable and a temporal lag on the dependent variable (no interaction of the two components) with the specification:

y_{it}=\lambdaWy_{it}  +  \rho y_{it-1} + x_{it}\beta + \eta_{i}+\epsilon_{it}

\eta_{i}  \sim iid (0, \sigma_{i})
\epsilon_{it} \sim iid(0, sigma_{it})

W is a block diagonal matrix.

We can contain a "slm" random effect component and a "ar1c" random effect component to fit this model, like

slmm1 <- inla( ln.CMEDV ~ -1 + CRIM + ZN + INDUS + CHAS + NOX2+ RM2 + AGE +
                 ln.DIS + ln.RAD + TAX + PTRATIO + B + ln.LSTAT +
                 f(idx, model="slm",
                   args.slm=list( rho.min = rho.min, rho.max = rho.max, W=W, X=mmatrix, Q.beta=Q.beta.spatial),
                   hyper=hyper) +
                    f(It, model = "ar1c",
                                             args.ar1c = list(Z =  mmatrix , Q.beta = Q.beta.temporal)),
               data=boston.c, family="gaussian",
               verbose=T,
               control.family = list(hyper=zero.variance),

Hi,

> If I understand well, for a dynamic model with both a spatial lag on the dependent variable and a temporal lag on the dependent variable (no interaction of the two components) with the specification:
>
> y_{it}=\lambdaWy_{it}  +  \rho y_{it-1} + x_{it}\beta + \eta_{i}+\epsilon_{it}
> \eta_{i}  \sim iid (0, \sigma_{i})
> \epsilon_{it} \sim iid(0, sigma_{it})

That model is equivalent to

y_{it} = (I - \lambdaW)^{-1} ( \rho y_{it-1} + x_{it}\beta + \eta_{i}+\epsilon_{it})

Hence, you have too many terms on the right hand side that the ’slm’ latent effect does not include. In particular, the term on y_{it-1} may be difficult to handle in INLA due to the structure it imposes on the models that it can fit. Please, define your model as

y_{it} = …

So that the right hand side does not depend on y_{it}. This will give you a better sense on the model that you are trying to fit and see if ti can be fit with INLA.

Best,

Virgilio

messages.subject_clean: INLA BYM model prior distribution definition.
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to estimate relative risk using the BYM model, where:
r_i: relative risk
y_i: observed cases
c_i: expected number of cases
And we assume that
y_i |r_i ∼ Poisson(c_i * exp{r_i})
r_i = Xβ+u_i +v_i.
where
u_i : spatial variability
v_i : non estructured variability
X : covariables matrix
β :  regression coefficients vector
and
β ∼ N(0,100)
π(u) ∝ exp{-SUM [w_ij  φ(u_i - u_j)]}
v ∼ N(0,100)
In order to run the model in R, I'm using the following formula:
formula <- round(yi) ~ 1 + cov1 + cov2 + cov3 + cov4 +
                         f(location, model = "bym", graph = poly2nb(map), scale.model = TRUE)

inla_model <- inla(formula, family = "poisson", data = data,
                   control.predictor = list(compute=T, link=1),
                   E = ci, control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE))

So, the question is: how can I change the prior beta parameters in the code, for example if I suppose a  N(-5,4) for the regression coefficients, ie, β ∼ N(-5,4).

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA BYM model prior distribution definition.
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] INLA BYM model prior distribution definition.
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

you can change the prior for the regression cooefs, see ?control.fixed,

with

y ~ 1 + x

you can say

	control.fixed=list(mean=list(x=1), prec=list(x=2))

meaning beta for x has N() prior with mean 1 and precision 2, just add
more if you have more

	control.fixed=list(mean=list(x=1,xx=2), prec=list(x=2,xx=3))

alternative, is the "linear" model, see

	inla.doc("linear")

so you can add

y ~ 1 + f(x, model="linear", mean.linear=1, prec.linear=2)

this is just another interface than 'control.fixed' and do the same.

Best
H
